# California, USA TRAVEL SURVIVAL KIT

**Traveler Types Covered**: Budget/Luxury/Family/Solo

## 1. SIM CARD SOLUTIONS

**Purpose**: Obtain local mobile connectivity for reliable navigation and communication.

| **Provider**          | **Details to Find**                                                         |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Verizon**           | Best nationwide coverage; Prepaid plans start at $35/mo (15GB)              |
| **T-Mobile**          | Excellent city speeds; Tourist "Connect" plans $15-$35/mo                   |
| **AT&T**              | Strong rural coverage; Prepaid plans around $30-$65/mo                      |
| **Data Allocation**   | Most plans offer 5GB to Unlimited; Throttling occurs after cap              |
| **Validity Period**   | Usually 30 days for prepaid kits                                            |
| **Hotspot/Tethering** | Allowed on most mid-tier plans                                              |
| **Where to Buy**      | Official stores, Best Buy, Target, CVS (Sim kits)                           |
| **Alternative: eSIM** | **Airalo**: ~$4.50 (1GB/7 days) to $26 (10GB/30 days) in USD                |

**Recommendations**:
- **Short trips (3-7 days)**: Use an eSIM (Airalo) for instant activation upon landing.
- **Longer stays (2+ weeks)**: A T-Mobile prepaid SIM provides the best balance of data and cost.
- **Road tripping National Parks**: Verizon is the gold standard for coverage in remote areas.

## 2. AIRPORT TRANSFERS

**Route**: From Los Angeles International (LAX) to Downtown LA / Santa Monica

| **Mode**                     | **Duration**       | **Cost**      | **Booking**                    | **Convenience** | **Best For**               |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------- | -------------------------- |
| **FlyAway Bus**              | 35–60 mins         | $9.75         | Online/Kiosk at Union Station  | Excellent       | Solo travelers, budget     |
| **Ride-hail (Uber/Lyft)**    | 40–90 mins         | $40–$70       | App (Must use LAX-it lot)      | Very Good       | Door-to-door, groups       |
| **Metro Rail (C-Line)**      | 60–80 mins         | $1.75         | TAP Card at station            | Moderate        | Extreme budget, light bags |
| **Hotel Shuttle**            | 30–50 mins         | Free/Varies   | Call hotel via courtesy phone  | Excellent       | Airport-area hotels        |
| **Car Rental**               | Variable           | $50+/day      | Online/Shuttle to remote lot   | Good            | State-wide exploration     |

**Details**:
- **Boarding Location**: Ride-hails and Taxis require a free shuttle to the "LAX-it" lot next to Terminal 1.
- **Frequency**: FlyAway buses depart every 30 minutes.
- **Operating Hours**: Most services run 24/7, though FlyAway has a gap between 1 AM and 5 AM.

**Current Exchange Rate**: 1 USD = Local Base Currency

| **Location**             | **Why It's Best**          | **Hours**       | **Rates**       | **Tips** |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- | -------- |
| **Major Banks (Chase)**  | Safest, official rates     | 9 AM – 5 PM     | Mid-market      | Need ID  |
| **Travelex (Malls)**     | Convenient in cities       | Mall hours      | Higher fees     | Avoid    |
| **ATM (Bank-affiliated)**| Most convenient/fair       | 24/7            | Best available  | Use Debit|

**Alternative Methods**:
- **ATM Withdrawal**: The standard way to get cash; check if your home bank has a "Global ATM Alliance" partner (e.g., Westpac/Barclays with Bank of America) to waive fees.
- **Credit Card**: California is highly cashless; Visa and Mastercard are accepted everywhere from food trucks to fine dining.

## 5. MUST-TRY FOODS

🍽️ **In-N-Out Burger** – Fast Food
- **What**: Cult-favorite burger chain using fresh, never-frozen ingredients.
- **Try with**: "Animal Style" burger and fries (Secret Menu).
- **Price**: $8–$12 for a meal.

🍽️ **Mission Burrito** – Mexican-American
- **What**: Giant, foil-wrapped burritos originating in San Francisco’s Mission District.
- **Where**: La Taqueria or El Farolito (SF).
- **Price**: $12–$15.

🍽️ **Avocado Toast** – California Fusion
- **What**: Fresh sourdough topped with local avocados, lemon, and chili flakes.
- **Where**: Any brunch spot in Los Angeles or San Diego.
- **Price**: $14–$20.

## 12. CUSTOMS & ETIQUETTE

Social norms in California are generally relaxed but governed by specific service-industry standards. Politeness and "laid-back" attitudes are the cultural default.

### 12a. Temple & Sacred Site Dress Code
Dress is casual in most religious sites, though modesty is appreciated in historic Missions.

| **Rule**                | **What to Check**                            | **Enforcement Level**           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Shoulders/Knees**     | Generally relaxed                            | Flexible                        |
| **Footwear**            | Keep shoes on unless stated                  | Standard                        |
| **Head covering**       | Rarely required                              | Minimal                         |

### 12b. The Head, Feet & Body — Cultural Hierarchy
Personal space is highly valued; avoid touching strangers or standing too close in queues.

### 12c. Interaction & Social Etiquette
Service staff expect friendly interaction, and eye contact is considered a sign of trustworthiness.

| **Rule**                         | **Detail**                                                             | **Who It Applies To** |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| **Tipping**                      | 18%-22% is the standard for sit-down service                           | All diners            |
| **Smoking**                      | Prohibited in almost all public buildings and parks                    | Everyone              |
| **Queueing**                     | Cutting in line is considered very offensive                           | All visitors          |

### 12d. Saving Face & Conflict Resolution
While not a "face" culture in the Asian sense, public scenes are frowned upon. Calmly asking for a manager is the standard way to resolve service disputes.

### 12e. Responsible Tourism & Environmental Welfare
Water conservation is a critical issue; travelers should follow "Leave No Trace" principles in National Parks and minimize plastic use.

### 12f. General Social Customs & Greetings
Handshakes are the standard greeting; "How are you?" is often used as a greeting rather than a literal question.

## 13. SAFETY & PRACTICAL INFORMATION

### 13a. Vaccinations & Preventative Health
No specific tropical vaccines are required for California.

| **Vaccine / Medication**           | **Priority Level**   | **Notes**                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Standard Boosters**              | Recommended          | Ensure Tetanus and Flu shots are current.                                                           |

### 13b. Insect Protection
Ticks in Northern California can carry Lyme disease; use repellent when hiking in tall grass.

### 13c. Water & Food Safety
Tap water is strictly regulated and safe to drink throughout the state.

| **Source**                  | **Safety**               | **Guidance**                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Tap water**               | Safe                     | Drinkable everywhere; bring a refillable bottle.                                                  |

### 13d. Personal Safety & Crime Awareness

California is generally safe for tourists, but urban centers have specific risks that require vigilance.

**ISSUE: Vehicle Burglary ("Bipping")**
**WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Especially prevalent in San Francisco (near Twin Peaks, Lombard St, and Fisherman's Wharf) and parts of Oakland and Los Angeles.
**HOW IT HAPPENS:** Thieves smash windows of parked cars—often in broad daylight—to grab bags or electronics. They target rentals specifically.
**HOW TO AVOID IT:** **Never leave anything visible in the car.** Even a jacket or a charging cable can trigger a break-in. Put all luggage in the hotel before sightseeing.
**WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS:** Do not confront the thieves; they are often in getaway cars. Call the local police non-emergency line to file a report for insurance.

**ISSUE: Homelessness & Mental Health Crisis**
**WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Tenderloin and SOMA districts in San Francisco; Skid Row and parts of Hollywood in Los Angeles.
**HOW IT HAPPENS:** Large encampments exist on sidewalks. While most individuals are harmless, some may be experiencing mental health episodes or drug-induced distress.
**HOW TO AVOID IT:** Stay on well-lit main streets. If you see someone acting erratically, give them a wide berth and do not engage or stare.
**WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS:** Walk away quickly. If you feel threatened, enter a nearby shop or restaurant.

**ISSUE: Bag Snatching & Pickpocketing**
**WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Crowded tourist hubs like the Hollywood Walk of Fame, Venice Beach Boardwalk, and Pier 39.
**HOW IT HAPPENS:** In crowded areas, thieves may lift wallets from back pockets or snatch phones held loosely.
**HOW TO AVOID IT:** Keep your phone in a front pocket or zipped bag. Be wary of "street performers" who draw large crowds or individuals who try to put "free" CDs or bracelets in your hand—they will demand money aggressively.

## 14. SEASONAL CONSIDERATIONS
California is a year-round destination, but weather varies wildly.
- **Wildfire Season (Aug-Nov)**: Air quality can drop significantly; check the "AirNow" app.
- **June Gloom**: Coastal areas (LA/SD) are often foggy and cool until mid-afternoon in early summer.
- **Winter**: SF and the North can be very rainy; the Sierra Nevada mountains require snow chains for cars.

## 15. GENERAL TIPS
- **Sales Tax**: The price on the tag is NOT the final price; expect 7.25% to 10.25% added at the register.
- **National Park Pass**: If visiting more than two parks (Yosemite, Joshua Tree, etc.), buy the "America the Beautiful" pass for $80.
- **Power Sockets**: Type A and B (120V). Bring a universal adapter if traveling from Europe or Asia.
